chunks: Asim ibn Humayd narrated from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

Whoever enters a marketplace or a congregational mosque and says once: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, alone, without any partner. Allah is the Greatest, immensely great. All praise belongs to Allah, abundantly. Glory be to Allah, morning and evening. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Most Great. And may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and his family. It is counted for him as an accepted Hajj.

key_terms.أَشْهَدُ: I bear witness; a declaration of faith
key_terms.الْعَلِيِّ الْعَظِيمِ: the Most High, the Most Great; divine attributes of Allah
key_terms.سُوقاً: a marketplace; a place of buying and selling
key_terms.لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ: He has no partner; affirmation of tawhid
key_terms.مَسْجِدَ جَمَاعَةٍ: a congregational mosque where people gather
key_terms.وَصَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَآلِهِ: may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and his family

ai.seo_question: What supplication should be recited when entering the marketplace or a congregational mosque, and what is its reward?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a dhikr and du'a to be recited upon entering a marketplace or a congregational mosque. It highlights the great reward attached to remembrance of Allah, tawhid, praise, glorification, and salawat upon Muhammad and his family, stating that it equals for the reciter an accepted Hajj.
